results.name: opp_parity_just_outside_yes
results.description: In sets of >=2 whose examples all share a parity, yes-rate for opposite-parity targets 1-3 outside the example span; observed below null means the model over-extends ranges to opposite-parity neighbours (people extrapolate by parity), above null means people extend magnitude ranges past the edge more than the model.
results.code:
# name: opp_parity_just_outside_yes
# description: In sets of >=2 whose examples all share a parity, yes-rate for opposite-parity targets 1-3 outside the example span; observed below null means the model over-extends ranges to opposite-parity neighbours (people extrapolate by parity), above null means people extend magnitude ranges past the edge more than the model.
def test_statistic(df):
    X = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.replace(" ", "", regex=False).str.split(",", expand=True)
    X = X.apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").values.astype(float)
    n = (~np.isnan(X)).sum(axis=1)
    mx = np.nanmax(X, axis=1)
    mn = np.nanmin(X, axis=1)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).values
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).values
    is_ex = (X == t[:, None]).any(axis=1)
    par = np.where(np.isnan(X), np.nan, np.mod(X, 2))
    allsame = np.nanmax(par, axis=1) == np.nanmin(par, axis=1)
    sp = np.nanmin(par, axis=1)
    dist = np.maximum(mn - t, t - mx)
    m = (n >= 2) & allsame & (dist >= 1) & (dist <= 3) & (np.mod(t, 2) != sp)
    return float(r[m].mean()) if m.any() else 0.0

results.name: parity_gap_inside_minus_outside
results.description: In sets of >=2 sharing a parity, (same-minus-opposite parity yes gap for non-example targets inside the span) minus (the same gap for targets outside the span); observed below null means people interpolate by magnitude but extrapolate by parity more than the model, above null means parity matters more inside the span than the model predicts.
results.code:
# name: parity_gap_inside_minus_outside
# description: In sets of >=2 sharing a parity, (same-minus-opposite parity yes gap for non-example targets inside the span) minus (the same gap for targets outside the span); observed below null means people interpolate by magnitude but extrapolate by parity more than the model, above null means parity matters more inside the span than the model predicts.
def test_statistic(df):
    X = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.replace(" ", "", regex=False).str.split(",", expand=True)
    X = X.apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").values.astype(float)
    n = (~np.isnan(X)).sum(axis=1)
    mx = np.nanmax(X, axis=1)
    mn = np.nanmin(X, axis=1)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).values
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).values
    is_ex = (X == t[:, None]).any(axis=1)
    par = np.where(np.isnan(X), np.nan, np.mod(X, 2))
    allsame = np.nanmax(par, axis=1) == np.nanmin(par, axis=1)
    sp = np.nanmin(par, axis=1)
    g = (n >= 2) & allsame & ~is_ex
    same = np.mod(t, 2) == sp
    ins = (t > mn) & (t < mx)
    out = (t < mn) | (t > mx)
    def gap(region):
        a = g & region & same
        b = g & region & ~same
        if a.sum() == 0 or b.sum() == 0:
            return 0.0
        return r[a].mean() - r[b].mean()
    return float(gap(ins) - gap(out))

results.name: set_size_near_outside_gap
results.description: Yes-rate for non-example targets 1-10 outside the span in sets of 3-4 examples minus the same in sets of 2; observed below null means more examples tighten generalization more than the model's size principle predicts, above null means people tighten less with more examples.
results.code:
# name: set_size_near_outside_gap
# description: Yes-rate for non-example targets 1-10 outside the span in sets of 3-4 examples minus the same in sets of 2; observed below null means more examples tighten generalization more than the model's size principle predicts, above null means people tighten less with more examples.
def test_statistic(df):
    X = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.replace(" ", "", regex=False).str.split(",", expand=True)
    X = X.apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").values.astype(float)
    n = (~np.isnan(X)).sum(axis=1)
    mx = np.nanmax(X, axis=1)
    mn = np.nanmin(X, axis=1)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).values
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).values
    is_ex = (X == t[:, None]).any(axis=1)
    dist = np.maximum(mn - t, t - mx)
    near = (dist >= 1) & (dist <= 10)
    a = near & (n >= 3)
    b = near & (n == 2)
    if a.sum() == 0 or b.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(r[a].mean() - r[b].mean())

results.name: below_asym_min_first
results.description: In sets of >=2, yes-rate for targets 1-10 below the min when the smallest example is shown first minus when it is not; the model has no first-shown cue, so observed below null means a first-shown minimum marks the range bottom (restricts downward extension), above null means it invites downward extension.
results.code:
# name: below_asym_min_first
# description: In sets of >=2, yes-rate for targets 1-10 below the min when the smallest example is shown first minus when it is not; the model has no first-shown cue, so observed below null means a first-shown minimum marks the range bottom (restricts downward extension), above null means it invites downward extension.
def test_statistic(df):
    X = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.replace(" ", "", regex=False).str.split(",", expand=True)
    X = X.apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").values.astype(float)
    n = (~np.isnan(X)).sum(axis=1)
    mx = np.nanmax(X, axis=1)
    mn = np.nanmin(X, axis=1)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).values
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).values
    is_ex = (X == t[:, None]).any(axis=1)
    first = X[:, 0]
    dn = (n >= 2) & (t < mn) & (t >= mn - 10)
    a = dn & (first == mn)
    b = dn & (first != mn)
    if a.sum() == 0 or b.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(r[a].mean() - r[b].mean())

results.name: singleton_far_yes
results.description: For single-example sets, yes-rate for targets more than 20 from the example; observed above null means people generalize broadly from one example (rule-based) more than the model, below null means the model over-produces far generalization from a single example.

results.name: trial_index_yes_corr
results.description: Correlation between trial_index (position in session) and yes response over non-example targets; observed below null means people say yes less as the session goes on (fatigue/conservatism drift absent from the model), above null means increasing yes bias.
results.code:
# name: trial_index_yes_corr
# description: Correlation between trial_index (position in session) and yes response over non-example targets; observed below null means people say yes less as the session goes on (fatigue/conservatism drift absent from the model), above null means increasing yes bias.
def test_statistic(df):
    X = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.replace(" ", "", regex=False).str.split(",", expand=True)
    X = X.apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").values.astype(float)
    n = (~np.isnan(X)).sum(axis=1)
    mx = np.nanmax(X, axis=1)
    mn = np.nanmin(X, axis=1)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).values
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).values
    is_ex = (X == t[:, None]).any(axis=1)
    ti = df["trial_index"].astype(float).values
    m = ~is_ex
    a = ti[m]
    y = r[m]
    if m.sum() < 3 or a.std() == 0 or y.std() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(np.corrcoef(a, y)[0, 1])

results.name: nonparity_rule_far_gap
results.description: In sets of >=2, among targets >10 outside the span, yes-rate for targets that share a non-parity rule (multiple of 3-12, last digit, contains digit, prime, square, cube) with all examples minus targets that share none; observed above null means people generalize by specific arithmetic rules far from the examples more than the model, below null means the model over-credits such rules.
results.code:
# name: nonparity_rule_far_gap
# description: In sets of >=2, among targets >10 outside the span, yes-rate for targets that share a non-parity rule (multiple of 3-12, last digit, contains digit, prime, square, cube) with all examples minus targets that share none; observed above null means people generalize by specific arithmetic rules far from the examples more than the model, below null means the model over-credits such rules.
def test_statistic(df):
    X = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.replace(" ", "", regex=False).str.split(",", expand=True)
    X = X.apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").values.astype(float)
    n = (~np.isnan(X)).sum(axis=1)
    mx = np.nanmax(X, axis=1)
    mn = np.nanmin(X, axis=1)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).values
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).values
    is_ex = (X == t[:, None]).any(axis=1)
    N = np.arange(101)
    rules = [N % k == 0 for k in range(3, 13)]
    rules += [N % 10 == d for d in range(1, 10)]
    s = np.array([str(i) for i in N])
    rules += [np.char.find(s, str(d)) >= 0 for d in range(1, 10)]
    pr = np.array([i > 1 and all(i % j for j in range(2, int(i ** 0.5) + 1)) for i in N])
    rules += [pr, np.isin(N, [1, 4, 9, 16, 25, 36, 49, 64, 81, 100]), np.isin(N, [1, 8, 27, 64])]
    M = np.array(rules)
    M[:, 0] = True
    Xi = np.nan_to_num(X, nan=0).astype(int)
    cons = M[:, Xi].all(axis=2)
    hit = (cons & M[:, t]).any(axis=0)
    dist = np.maximum(mn - t, t - mx)
    g = (n >= 2) & (dist > 10)
    a = g & hit
    b = g & ~hit
    if a.sum() == 0 or b.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(r[a].mean() - r[b].mean())

results.name: cell_unanimity_rate
results.description: Fraction of (set, target) cells with >=5 responses in which all responses agree (all yes or all no); observed above null means people's per-item yes probabilities are more extreme than the model's (model too noisy/hedged), below null means people are less consistent across participants than the model.
results.code:
# name: cell_unanimity_rate
# description: Fraction of (set, target) cells with >=5 responses in which all responses agree (all yes or all no); observed above null means people's per-item yes probabilities are more extreme than the model's (model too noisy/hedged), below null means people are less consistent across participants than the model.
def test_statistic(df):
    X = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.replace(" ", "", regex=False).str.split(",", expand=True)
    X = X.apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").values.astype(float)
    n = (~np.isnan(X)).sum(axis=1)
    mx = np.nanmax(X, axis=1)
    mn = np.nanmin(X, axis=1)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).values
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).values
    is_ex = (X == t[:, None]).any(axis=1)
    key = df["number_set"].astype(str).values + "|" + df["target"].astype(str).values
    codes, inv = np.unique(key, return_inverse=True)
    cnt = np.bincount(inv)
    s = np.bincount(inv, weights=r)
    ok = cnt >= 5
    if not ok.any():
        return 0.0
    un = (s[ok] == 0) | (s[ok] == cnt[ok])
    return float(un.mean())
